summary: Verified CR-385 alert-bar '+N more' popover behavior on cr385-frontdesk-mockup.html. All 5 acceptance criteria pass: alert-bar shows 3 items + '+3 more' link; clicking alert-more opens alert-popover with header 'All alerts · 6' and exactly 6 alert-item-<i> rows (3 in bar + 3 in +more); toggle click closes popover; outside click closes popover; repeated open/close cycles produce no duplicate popovers (always 1); row click navigates and expands the correct record and closes popover; zero JS console errors captured throughout.

issues: Row 0 label reads 'K. Menon · stay expired, not arrived' but clicking it opens the Check-In record for 'D. Naik' (BK-3006). Since all data is MOCKED this may be intentional stub linkage, but the name mismatch between alert label and expanded record looks inconsistent to a reviewer. Worth confirming the mock go(tab,chip,id) target IDs align with alert labels.

action_items: (Optional) Align mocked alert labels with the IDs they navigate to so the row-click destination matches the alert text (e.g., K. Menon alert should expand K. Menon's booking, not D. Naik).
critical_code_review_comments: Popover create/remove logic is clean: only one #alertpop node exists at a time even after rapid toggles (verified via querySelectorAll count = 1).
Row count invariant (3 in bar + N from '+N more' == popover row count) held true (3+3=6).
Outside-click and toggle-close both wired correctly; no leaked event listeners observed across 3 toggle cycles.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Only the alert '+N more' popover was in scope for iteration_15. Full v2.18 booking suite was intentionally not re-run per E1 instruction. If retesting, use the same public URL and viewport 1920x800; assert popover row count equals 3 + int(match on '+N more'). Note the (likely mocked) label/record mismatch on row 0 flagged under design_issues.
